potential_defenses: The login logic code completes the full validation of the username and password before returning a response.

technique_name: L6.6.4 Remote Timing Attack > L6.6.4.3 RSA OEAP Padding Attack

detection_opportunities: Randomly input ciphertext into the RSA OAEP decryption interface, and record the response time. Compare this response time with that of normal ciphertext. If the response time is significantly shorter than the normal response time, a vulnerability exists.

technique_name: C6.1.1 Exploiting the K8s Platform to Steal Credentials > C6.1.1.1 K8s secret disclosure
description:
The ServiceAccount token is the identity credential used by the processes in the pod of the Kubernetes cluster. If RBAC is not enabled in the cluster, the ServiceAccount token has high permissions and can be used to fully control the cluster. If the token is disclosed, the damage is great.
Check method:
1. Run the kubectl get pod -o wide -A command to check the pods on the host machine.
2. Use the name and namespace of the pod to be tested obtained in step 1 and run the kubectl exec -it Pod name -n namespace --bash command to enter the container.

technique_name: C6.1.1 Exploiting the K8s Platform to Steal Credentials > C6.1.1.4 Using the K8s Access Controller to steal information
description:
After obtaining the cluster-admin permission, an attacker can create a malicious access controller to hook all API accesses and reference the attacker's external webhook as the validating service. In this way, K8S sends API requests carrying sensitive information to an external server.
Take the K8S as an example:
1. Run the netstat -pantu command on the host machine.
grep -i listen
Run the grep kube-api command to view the IP address and port number of the APIServer.
2. Run the kubectl get pod -o wide -A command to check the pods on the host machine.
3. Use the pod name and namespace to be tested in step 2 and run the kubectl exec -it Pod name -n namespace --bash command to enter the container.
4. In the container, run the curl https://192.168.31.220:4443/version -H "Authorization:Bearer $token" -k -v command to check whether the K8S information can be obtained.
In the preceding command, https://192.168.31.220:4443 indicates the API server information obtained in step 1.
potential_defenses: Apply least privilege access controls
Monitor and audit credential access activities
detection_opportunities: 1. Check whether the admission controller is abnormal.
code_examples_patterns: kubectl exec into pod and read /run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token

technique_name: C6.1.2 Leakage of Service Credentials with the Carrier > C6.1.2.1 Application-Layer API Credential Disclosure
description:
In complex service scenarios and microservice architectures, Kubernetes services, containers and VMs, and containers communicate with each other through APIs. Communication credentials can be stolen for horizontal penetration.
Take the K8S as an example:
1. Run the kubectl get pod -o wide -A command to check the pods on the host machine.
2. Use the name and namespace of the pod to be tested obtained in step 1 and run the kubectl exec -it Pod name -n namespace --bash command to enter the container.
2. Run the find / -name "session" command in the container to check whether the host machine certificate can be obtained.
potential_defenses: Apply least privilege access controls
Monitor and audit credential access activities
detection_opportunities: 1. Leakage of API credentials at the application layer
